per_window.ps-ns: dynamic_in_window at the termini and loops, with ordered tryptophans and catalytic carboxylates of restricted amplitude. Free WT, pD 6.2: catalytic side chains S2 0.64-0.75 (J1, r1), matched in trend by MD (J8). Free WT, pH 5.5: Trp indoles S2 0.83-0.92 and handle backbone 0.84 ± 0.01 (J2, measured_not_detected). RelaxDB source paper (Yamasaki et al. 1995, full text; free WT, 27 °C, pH 5.5, 100 mM acetate, 600 MHz): dynamic_in_window; tau_R 10.92 ns, S2 0.15-1.0 (average 0.85), large motion at L2-K3, C13-G15, E61-H62, D70-S71, A93-K96, G123-H127, Q152-V155 with tau_e 0.45-2.2 ns (J38, E-r1); the 47 class I amides of helices and strands show no enhanced fast motion (J51, no_evidence_in_window); the paper's 300 ps MD reproduces most order parameters (J53, md_only). Reanalyses of published backbone and methyl data: C-terminal V153/V155 methyls have low, model-sensitive S2axis (J44); per-residue S2 and local tau_m rosters are figure-only (J45). MD (2 mus) reproduces the order parameters (J46, md_only). Cysteine-free RNase HI*: extra fast motion at L2, M50, A63, V153, V155 methyls (J4) and tau_s above 300 ps in loops and termini (J5); ILV methyl local correlation times 7-14 ns (J3). Quintuple mutant restricts K96 and V98 (J41, abstract). iG80b keeps ordered indoles (J6); the thermophilic homolog has a more mobile W81 (J7).
per_window.us-ms: Reference state (free WT, 27 °C, pH 5.5, 600 MHz, RelaxDB source paper, full text): exchange detected but unresolved by the single-field rule: 21 amides need a model-free Δex term, concentrated in helices I (M50, A51, A52, A55, L56, L59) and IV (V101, D102, D103, W104, L107, A109, A110, L111) plus I78, I82, W90 (2.61 Hz, the largest), K91, N100, W118 and E135, mean Δex 0.71 Hz, read by the authors as millisecond exchange and possibly cooperative helix motion; no rate, population or second peak set (J52, E-r2). Other constructs: dynamic_in_window in the substrate-binding handle of the free enzyme, with no rate or population. Methyl Hahn-echo at 14.1 T, pH 5.5: V98, V101 and L103 are broadened beyond the exchange-free reference at 283, 300 and 310 K, read as open-closed exchange of the handle, with I78 and I82 elevated at 283 K; apparent activation energies 45.4 ± 1.6 (V98) and 23.7 ± 1.9 kJ/mol (V101) under a fast-limit two-site assumption (J47, 2019, full text). Multifield backbone reanalysis: 40 amides with Rex above 1 s-1 at 21.15 T, G77 4.00 ± 0.38 s-1 at 900 MHz, roster figure-only (J18, 2026, full text). Abstract-level: helix I exchange contribution in WT (J42) that is reduced, while the protrusion junction gains exchange, in the quintuple mutant (J43). Indirect: model-free Rex at V54 and G77 in RNase HI* (J19); Mg2+-induced R1rho broadening inseparable from Mg2+ binding (J20). Refolding phases of 120 mus and 3.1 ms (J21) and variant folding phases (J22) are folding intermediates. Caveat for every full-text us-ms row: the 2019, 2024 and 2026 articles do not restate the sample's cysteine content, so whether the measured protein is the entry sequence or cysteine-free RNase HI* is unconfirmed.
per_window.slower_than_ms: search_insufficient for free WT (J37): no method gives a slower-than-ms rate for the folded enzyme. A folding model gives a 0.78 s-1 Icore-to-native step (J23). Native-state H/D exchange is measured only in I53A (J24) and, abstract only, in D10A (J25); acid-induced non-native states keep helix I protected (J49, abstract); pulsed-labeling HX-MS refolding of ecRNH*, A55G and D108L orders helix A before helix D (J50, other construct).
per_window.undetermined: Handle loop: RDCs and V101 rotamers of free WT fit open/closed averaging, with E. coli the most open homolog and a V101 trans rotamer of about 10% (J11, r18, indirect); V98A shifts toward closed (J12, J13); homolog RDC ordering (J14). MD: WT G15 minor backbone state 39% (J9), handle open/closed in WT (J10), 2 mus OPLS4/AMBER runs decomposing methyl order at L2, L59, I116, V153, V155 (J46), MD abstracts (J39; the 1995 MD is now full text in J53), iG80b W81 rotamer switch (J15), homologs (J16), alchemical MSlambdaD (J17). NMR-ensemble side-chain heterogeneity partly attributed to structure-determination artefacts (J40). Structures: metal positions differ among Mg2+ crystal forms (J26) and H124 binds Zn2+ through different nitrogens (J27); SSB-Ct pocket expansion (J28); SSB-Ct titration peak loss (J29, binding); B factors (J30), metal-bound (J31), mutant (J32, J33) abstracts; I53A crystal keeps the fold (J34). smFRET rows report enzyme-substrate binding and degradation (J35, J36). H124 catalytic side-chain change proposed from kinetics (J48). Not judged from the 2026-10-20 re-read (D-rN = RNASEHI-RNASEHI_20261020150655-rN): the preprint version of the 2019 methyl paper (D-r20, not independent); alanine-scanning kinetics and CD of handle variants (D-r23, no dynamics measurement); pulsed-labeling and competition HX-MS refolding of the Thermus homolog, its CD chevrons and the reconstructed ancestors Anc1-Anc3 and AncA-AncD (D-r29 to r38, homologs, folding).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes, exchange is detected in the reference state but without a rate or population: in the RelaxDB source sample (free wild-type E. coli RNase HI, 27 °C, pH 5.5, 100 mM acetate, 600 MHz, single field) 21 backbone amides need a model-free exchange term, concentrated in helices I (M50-L56, L59) and IV (V101-A110, L111) plus I78, I82, W90, K91, N100, W118 and E135, mean Δex 0.71 Hz and 2.61 Hz at W90 (J52, full text); single-field Rex can also come from anisotropic tumbling, so the call is 'possible' and a dispersion experiment would confirm. The handle-region exchange with temperature dependence (V98, V101, L103; G77 Rex 4.00 ± 0.38 s-1 at 900 MHz) is measured in cysteine-free RNase HI* (J47, J18). Fast motion in the reference state sits in the termini and five loops (S2 down to 0.14-0.15, tau_e 0.45-2.2 ns; J38) and is restricted in the secondary structure (J51).
open_conflicts: Catalytic side-chain S2: NMR 0.64-0.75 at D10, E48, D70, D134 (pD 6.2) versus MD 0.76-0.85 (r1 versus r3); the authors attribute the gap to protonation averaging near the D10 pKa and force-field limits.
The 2013 paper names N44 in the Mg2+ group-1 broadening set and N45 in the conservation text (r2 versus r1); kept as printed.

Construct identity of the us-ms evidence: the 2019 methyl, 2024 JCTC and 2026 JACS articles (D-r9 to r19) are labelled 'target' in the evidence but never restate the cysteine content of the sample, while the same laboratory's 2018 methyl sample (r25) is called cysteine-free by the 2025 paper (r26); if these samples are RNase HI*, J18, J44, J45 and J47 become inference_from_mutant and the wt_apo_answer drops to the earlier 'not established'.

Residue 71 in the 1995 abstract (D-r1): the abstract writes Asp70-Tyr71 while the entry sequence has S71 and Y73; both second readers flagged the row, the corrected row keeps Tyr71 as printed, and J38 maps D70 only.

Residue letters in the 1995 paper: Ala131 and Asp103 (p. 6591, class lists; Glu131 on p. 6599), Tyr71 (flexible-loop text; Ser71 in the class III list) and Asn43/Asp92 (MD discussion) differ from the entry E131, L103, S71, T43, T92; the rows keep the printed letters and map by number (adjudication ledger/adjudication_pdf_batch1.json).
questions_for_gina: Which sample is the RelaxDB RNASEHI R1/R2/NOE set, and are the Palmer-laboratory samples in the 2019 methyl-exchange, 2024 JCTC and 2026 JACS papers the Cys-containing wild type (the entry sequence) or the cysteine-free RNase HI*? The answer decides whether the us-ms handle exchange (J47, J18) counts as reference-state evidence.

The 1995 source paper (full text) detects exchange only as a single-field model-free Δex term at 21 amides (helices I and IV, W90 largest), with no rate or population. Does single-field Rex count as us-ms exchange for the alternate-APO call (applied here as 'possible' with the anisotropic-tumbling caveat), and should the earlier 15N handle-exchange studies cited as refs 54-56 of the 2019 paper be added in full?
